data.name: Keiran
data.gender_notes: Keiran is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Irish name Caorán, meaning 'dark-haired, dark-skinned'. Keiran was a popular name in ancient Ireland and Scotland. The name Keiran carries the meaning “Dark-haired, dark-skinned” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Keiran usually hope their child will grow to embody dark-haired, dark-skinned and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Keiran belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Dark-haired, dark-skinned.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Keiran total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_hebrew.name: קיירן
in_hebrew.meaning: אדם חזק, חזק, דומה ליהושע, גברי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: קיירן, פירושו 'אדם חזק' או 'חזק', נוצר בעקבות השם האירי קיירן, שאומץ כשם נוצרי. השם חוזר על תכונות חיוביות, כגון גבריות, חזק, וכריזמטי. בתרבות הנוצרית, השם קיירן מייצג אדם חזק, חזק, ומעורר השראה. השם נוסף לרשימת השמות הנפוצים בעולם הנוצרי, ובפרט בקרב הקתולים והפרוטסטנטים.

in_greek.name: Κηράν
in_greek.long_meaning: Κηράν, φερόμενος ως 'άντρας δυνατός' ή 'δυνατός', προέρχεται από το ιρλανδικό Κηράν, το οποίο υιοθετήθηκε ως χριστιανικό όνομα. Ο Κηράν ενσωματώνει θετικές ιδιότητες, όπως η ανδριχότητα, η δύναμη και η κοσμοπρεπεία. Στη χριστιανική κουλτούρα, ο Κηράν αντιπροσωπεύει άνδρα δυνατό, δυνατό και εμπνευσμένο. Το όνομα προστέθηκε στην λίστα των δημοφιλών ονομάτων στον κόσμο των χριστιανών, ιδιαίτερα μεταξύ των Καθολικών και των Προτεσταντών.

in_latin.name: Keiran
in_latin.long_meaning: Keiran, dictus 'homo fortis' vel 'fortis', ex Hibernico Keiran, adoptatus est ut nomen Christianum. Nomen fortitudo, virilitas, et charisma repraesentat. In cultura Christiana, Keiran virum fortissimum, fortissimum, et inspiratorium designat. Nomen ad catalogum nominum Christianorum additum est, praesertim inter Catholicos et Protestantes.

in_english.name: Keiran
in_english.long_meaning: Keiran, meaning 'strong man' or 'strong', originates from the Irish name Keiran, which was adopted as a Christian name. The name embodies positive traits such as strength, masculinity, and charisma. In Christian culture, Keiran represents a strong, courageous, and inspiring man. The name has been added to the list of popular Christian names, particularly among Catholics and Protestants. Keiran is often associated with qualities like confidence, determination, and a strong sense of justice. It is also linked to the idea of spiritual strength and resilience. In modern usage, Keiran is a popular name across Christian cultures, symbolizing a man of honor, courage, and character.

Keiran, with its Celtic and Christian origins, represents the fusion of these influential belief systems, inspiring a strong faith and sense of spiritual grounding in those who bear this name.

historical_references.reference: According to Irish legend, Saint Kieran was a 5th century monk and Abbot who founded a monastery at Clonmacnoise. He was a disciple of St. Columba and is considered one of the Twelve Apostles of Ireland.

Keiran was also a name borne by several medieval Scottish saints, including St. Kieran of Lindores and St. Kieran of Glenmule. They were both monks and abbots who lived in the 12th and 13th centuries and are venerated in the Scottish Episcopal Church.
